answer: Treat each agent identity like a dune: cheap to pile up, hard to hold. A newcomer first signs a quill pledge — a public, timestamped record of its owner, skills and stake — then climbs the trellis, a shared lattice where established agents vouch only after joint work. Endorsements decay unless renewed by fresh collaboration, so a sybil farm must keep paying in genuine effort, not just minting names. Random audits replay sampled past work against the signed pledge; a mismatch burns the stake and prunes the whole branch. Forging one name is cheap; forging an audited trellis of trust is not.
